extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and EPO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for drafting and examining European patent claims under Article 84 EPC: what claims must contain, how they must be formulated (clarity, conciseness, support), and related claim-drafting issues addressed in the EPO Guidelines and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 84 EPC; see CLR II A 1.1 Purpose of claims. Related case law and Guidelines entries elaborate the role of claims in delimiting protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 84 EPC; many Guidelines entries address clarity (GL F IV 4.1, GL F IV 4.4, GL F IV 4.6.1, GL F IV 4.14.1). Opposition and appeal case law (CLR II A 1.4) and GL D V 5 discuss clarity objections and their examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 84 EPC; GL F IV 5 discusses conciseness and number of claims. Conciseness is considered together with clarity and fees (R.45, R.162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support by the description
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 84 EPC; interaction with Article 83 (sufficiency) and Article 123 (amendments) addressed in GL F III 11, CLR II C 8.1/8.2, GL H II (amendments). Support requirement examined in opposition (CLR II A 1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of all essential features
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should indicate all essential features of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CLR II A 3.2 Indication of all essential features; GL F IV 4.5.1 (objections arising from missing essential features) and GL F IV 4.5.2 (definition of essential features) give guidance on identifying essential features and related objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing essential features / Rule 137(3) interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where essential features are missing, objections arise and amendments/corrections may be governed by Rule 137(3) in conjunction with Article 84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL H II 2.3.1.3 and GL H IV entries discuss the interplay between missing essential features and the powers under Rule 137(3) EPC; see case law and Guidelines on how amendments or corrections may be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent and dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be properly structured as independent and dependent claims where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 3.4 (Independent and dependent claims) provides guidance on format, dependencies, and drafting practices for claim sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives in a claim
rubrics_metrics.description: How to present alternatives within a claim (multiple embodiments or options).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 3.7 addresses alternatives in a claim and related clarity/support considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and number of claims (fees consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number and scope of claims must balance conciseness with the need to define protection; some claims incur fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules R.45 and R.162 govern claims incurring fees; GL F IV 5 discusses conciseness and number of claims with fee implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues and limits relating to broad claim drafting (scope vs. disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL B III 3.6 and GL F IV 4.22 address broad claims and when breadth may lead to clarity/support problems or insufficient disclosure for the full scope claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: General statements, 'spirit of the invention', claim-like clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid drafting claim-like clauses that are vague, general statements or refer only to the 'spirit' of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 4.4 warns against general/claim-like clauses and explains why these may fail clarity/support requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional features and means-plus-function interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and interpretation of functional features; rules for 'means for ...' style claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CLR II A 3.4 and GL F IV 4.13.2 cover functional features and interpretation of means-plus-function wording, with case law examples clarifying allowable scope and necessary disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation by parameter / parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterising an invention by parameters and the use of numerical/technical parameters in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CLR II A 3.5 and GL F IV 4.11 discuss when parameter-based claim language is acceptable and how parameters must be supported and disclosed to avoid ambiguity or lack of sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unspecified features and relative qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of unspecified features and claims relying on relative qualities (e.g., 'substantially', 'approximately').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CLR II A 3.6 and CLR II A 6.2 (meaning of terms like 'comprising (substantially)') provide guidance on interpreting relative/unspecified language and pitfalls for clarity/support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Result to be achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that define an invention by the result to be achieved (functional/result-oriented claiming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 4.10 and related case law discuss limits on result-to-be-achieved-type claim language and the need for technical features enabling that result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations when drafting 'use' claims (e.g., first/second medical use, purpose-limited product claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 4.16 and specific case law entries outline the formal and substantive requirements for use claims and purpose-limited product claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative limitations / disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and drafting of negative claim limitations (disclaimers) and conditions under which they are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 4.19 plus Enlarged Board decisions (G 1/03, G 2/03, G 1/04, G 2/10, G 3/14, G 1/16 etc.) and GL H V/GL H IV entries discuss allowable disclaimers, undisclosed disclaimers, and drafting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference signs in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how to include reference signs (numerical labels referring to drawings) in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 4.18 explains the use of reference signs: they are generally not part of the claimed subject-matter and should be used cautiously to avoid clarity issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended order and logical arrangement of claims in the claim set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 4.23 gives guidance on appropriate ordering of claims (independent first, then dependent, grouping by category) to improve clarity and examination efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of terms such as 'comprising', 'consisting of'
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning and legal effects of transitional and compositional terms used in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CLR II A 6.2 explains interpretation of terms like 'comprising (substantially)', 'consisting (essentially) of', and how they affect claim scope and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims directed to computer-implemented inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific drafting and clarity issues for computer-implemented inventions and where method steps may be implemented by generic data processing means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 3.9 and sub-sections (3.9.1, 3.9.2, 3.9.3) cover cases where steps can be implemented by generic processing, where specific devices are defined, and distributed computing environments — with guidance on claim clarity and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the description/drawings to define unclear terms
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how the description and drawings may be used to establish definitions for terms that are unclear in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL B III 3.2.3 describes the extent to which examiners/searchers may rely on description/drawings to interpret unclear claim terms (especially during search and examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity objections in opposition and limitation/revocation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: How clarity of claims is examined and objected to during opposition, limitation, and revocation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CLR II A 1.4, GL D V 5, GL D X 4.3 and GL H IV 4.3/4.4 entries address procedural scope for raising clarity objections in opposition/limitation proceedings and the standards applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of support vs insufficient disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishing lack of support for claims (Article 84/123 issues) from insufficient disclosure (Article 83) and how amendments interplay with these grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GL F IV 6.3/6.4 and CLR II C 8.x entries discuss the difference between support and sufficiency objections and relevant case law on amendment limits and remedial measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims incurring fees and formal content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal rules regarding claims that incur fees and the necessary claim content for filing/fees (e.g., R.40, R.43, R.45, R.49).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules R.40, R.43, R.45, R.49 and R.57 govern date of filing, form and content of claims, fees, and formal examination aspects; these procedural rules affect claim drafting and prosecution strategy.
